While the business unit name changed, the current disclosure's focus on mid-tier/enterprise OEM data center clients represents the specific counterpart segment to the general CNBU definition in 2024, particularly regarding the storage/DRAM mix for these customers. comparisons.peer_summary: AMD's four reportable segments are Data Center, Client, Gaming, and Embedded, each encompassing specific product lines for data centers, client devices, gaming hardware, and embedded solutions.
comparisons.comparison: Both disclosures define the specific product compositions and scope of their primary data center business units. MU's CNBU includes memory technologies like HBM, DDR, and CXL for data centers, while AMD's Data Center segment includes AI accelerators, server CPUs, and DPUs. Both serve the same end market (data center) but focus on different hardware components (memory vs. processing/acceleration).
